terrain-chunks.html.title: | Hex Terrains Framework
terrain-chunks.html.summary: Here is the documentation section for the Chunks Grid System in your Hex Terrains Framework: 🧩 Chunks Grid System The Hex Terrains Framework divides the terrain into chunks to enable efficient rendering, visibility culling, and simulation scaling. The Chunks Grid System manages the lifecycle, visibility state, and dynamic spatial organization of these chunks. Overview Each terrain is split into a grid of chunks. This system ensures: Only visible chunks are rendered or in some cases even updated. Chunks can dynamically adjust their transform offsets for seamless terrain tiling. Simulation and rendering can be constrained to active areas based on camera visibility. Core Concepts ChunksGridData A component that stores all spatial data related to chunk organization and visibility. It holds: Chunk settings (dimensions, count, etc.) Visibility flags per chunk (ChunkVisibility) Chunk metrics (ChunkMetrics) Dirty flags for dependency management and selective updating Added by: CreateChunksGridDataSystem ChunkBounds Each chunk tracks 9 bounds: Bounds_Center — actual location Bounds_{Direction} — adjacent bounds used for edge wrapping These enable neighborhood queries and visual interpolation across chunk edges. ChunkVisibility Stores per-chunk visibility information: IsVisible — true if inside camera frustum VisualPosition — where the chunk is currently rendered (may differ from actual world position if terrain wraps) ChunkOffset — logical offset used for virtual terrain scrolling Transform — final transform matrix applied to the chunk renderer Lifecycle Systems ✅ CreateChunksGridDataSystem Group: CreateHexTerrainsGroup Automatically adds ChunksGridData component to any entity with CreateChunksGridDataRequest Initializes chunk data using terrain settings chunksGridData.Init(request.Settings); 📐 CalcChunkVisibilitySystem Group: HexTerrainsInitializationGroup Recalculates visible chunks each frame based on camera frustum Stores new visibility states in ChunkVisibility per chunk Uses a CalcHexChunkVisibilityJob to run visibility culling in parallel var job = new CalcHexChunkVisibilityJob { // Assign metrics, frustum, visibility maps... }; job.Schedule(terrainSettings.ChunksCount, 16, combinedDeps); This system is the core of terrain culling and selective rendering. 🧹 CleanupChunksGridDataSystem Group: HexTerrainsCleanupGroup Calls CleanupAsync() on ChunksGridData when terrain is visible Authoring Support ChunksGridDataAuthoring Used in the Unity Editor to define chunks grid metadata Extracts terrain settings from a referenced HexTerrainAuthoring On bake, converts this to a CreateChunksGridDataRequest via ChunksGridDataBaker Execution Order Summary System Group Purpose CreateChunksGridDataSystem CreateHexTerrainsGroup Initializes chunks on terrain load CalcChunkVisibilitySystem HexTerrainsInitializationGroup Recomputes which chunks are visible CleanupChunksGridDataSystem HexTerrainsCleanupGroup Cleans up chunk data when no longer needed

terrain-layers.html.title: 🧱 Terrain Layers Overview | Hex Terrains Framework
terrain-layers.html.summary: 🧱 Terrain Layers Overview What is a Terrain Layer? In the Hex Terrains Framework, each terrain entity consists of several Terrain Layers, each responsible for managing a specific kind of spatial data or functionality over the hex grid. These layers are modular, extensible, and powered by job-safe DataLayer components. All layers share a common pattern: Store core data per-cell or per-chunk using DataLayers. Optionally include color maps for visualization and minimaps. Support reinitialization, cleanup, and job completion workflows. 🌍 Terrain Layer Types There are four primary layer types included in the framework: Layer Type Purpose Example Class SurfaceLayer Defines core physical terrain (height, biome, surface mesh) HexGroundLayer AreasLayer Stores area/country/province indices per cell HexCountriesLayer CellItemsLayer Stores static objects per cell, renderable with instancing CellItemPropsLayer CellEntitiesLayer Stores a full ECS entity per cell CellEntityPropsLayer 🟫 Surface Layer Represents visible terrain features like land or water. Key Features: Stores HeightMapDataLayer and CellBiomesDataLayer Contains a CellColorsDataLayer for visual overlays Linked to a HexSurfaceRenderLayer<T> for rendering Example: HexGroundLayer This is a simple implementation of HexSurfaceLayer for ground terrain. [ChunkSerializable] public partial class HexGroundLayer : HexSurfaceLayer, IComponentData { } Render Data Paired with HexGroundRenderLayer, which inherits HexSurfaceRenderLayer<HexGroundLayer> and handles: Mesh generation from data layers Material configs per view mode Dirty flag tracking and cleanup 🧱 Areas Layer Used to mark cells with region identifiers, such as provinces or countries. Example: HexCountriesLayer public partial class HexCountriesLayer : HexByteAreasLayer, IComponentData { } Internally uses: NativeListChunkedDataLayer<byte> for area indices CellColorsDataLayer for coloring each area 🧍 Cell Items Layer Stores static renderable objects per cell using GPU instancing (Graphics.DrawMeshInstanced). Key Components: CellItemDataLayer – index into a shared list of item types CellTransformDataLayer – transformation matrix per cell ItemsColorMap – overlay color per item RenderEntitiesConfig – defines instancing behavior RenderEntities – stores active render entity instances Example: CellItemPropsLayer public class CellItemPropsLayer : CellItemsLayer, IComponentData { } Utility Methods: SetCellItem(cellIndex, item) SetAllCellsItem(item) Init(settings, copyItemConfigsFrom, renderConfig) Resize(newSize) Dispose() Render Pipeline: Cell items are rendered based on their index and corresponding RenderEntitySettings. 🧬 Cell Entities Layer Stores an entire ECS entity per cell, useful for dynamic agents, buildings, or gameplay units. Example: CellEntityPropsLayer [ChunkSerializable] public class CellEntityPropsLayer : CellEntitiesLayer, IComponentData, IDisposable { } Each cell can store: A reference to a full entity A color (via CellColorsDataLayer) A transform if needed Like other layers, it implements: Init() SetAllDirty(bool) Cleanup(), CleanupAsync() CompleteAllJobs() 🎨 Color Maps Every layer includes a CellColorsDataLayer or ItemsColorMap, which stores per-cell Color32 values to: Support terrain visual overlays Fill GPU textures used in terrain materials or minimaps Provide diagnostic feedback in the editor To apply the color map: public void ApplyColorsToTexture(Texture2D texture, CellColorsDataLayer colorsDataLayer) { colorsDataLayer.ApplyColorsToTexture(Texture2D texture); } 🔁 Lifecycle Hooks Each TerrainLayer supports: Initialization (Init) Resizing (Resize) Dirty flag control (SetAllDirty(bool)) Cleanup (Cleanup, CleanupAsync) Disposal (Dispose) Job sync (CompleteAllJobs) These ensure safe parallel updates and smooth interoperation with Unity’s ECS and Jobs system. ✅ Summary Feature Surface Areas Items Entities Height & Biome ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ Area Index (byte) ❌ ✅ ❌ ❌ Static Rendered Objects ❌ ❌ ✅ ❌ Dynamic ECS Entities ❌ ❌ ❌ ✅ Cell Color Map ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Render Mesh Support ✅ ❌ ✅ ❌

terrain-serialization.html.title: Terrain Serialization and Deserialization | Hex Terrains Framework
terrain-serialization.html.summary: Terrain Serialization and Deserialization 📦 HexTerrainSerializer The HexTerrainSerializer is a static utility class that provides serialization and deserialization functionality for HexTerrain entities in the framework. It is used to persist terrain state to disk and restore it later. This is especially useful for save/load systems, debugging, world editors, or network transfers. It supports: Versioning for backward compatibility Standard and custom component serialization Flexible stream or file-based operations ✨ Features Serializes terrain settings and selected managed components. Supports custom serialization logic via user-provided callbacks. Backward-compatible versioning system for future-proofing saved data. Works entirely with ECS-friendly components and native containers. 🧠 Serializer Structure public static class HexTerrainSerializer This class contains all the logic needed to serialize and deserialize a terrain entity. public static class HexTerrainSerializer 🧾 Versioning public static int Version = 1; Indicates the serialization format version. Future versions may include additional data layers or structural changes. 💾 Saving Terrain SaveTerrainToFile public static bool SaveTerrainToFile(string filePath, Entity terrainEntity, EntityManager entityManager, CustomSerializerCallback customSerializer) Saves the terrain to a specified file. Internally calls Serialize. 🔄 Serialization There are three main overloads for serialization: Serialize(Stream stream, Entity terrainEntity, EntityManager entityManager, CustomSerializerCallback customSerializer) Serialize(BinaryWriter writer, Entity terrainEntity, EntityManager entityManager, CustomSerializerCallback customSerializer) WriteVersion1(BinaryWriter writer, Entity terrainEntity, EntityManager entityManager, CustomSerializerCallback customSerializer) Writes the current version number. Writes terrain settings using WriteTerrainSettings. Enumerates all managed components and serializes recognized types: HexSurfaceLayer CellItemsLayer CellEntitiesLayer HexByteAreasLayer Supports custom serialization logic by invoking the CustomSerializerCallback. Supported Layer Writers: WriteSurfaceData WriteCellItemsData WriteCellEntitiesData WriteTerrainByteAreas Component Type Resolution TypeHash.CalculateStableTypeHash(componentType.GetManagedType()) Used to store the component type in a format that’s stable and consistent. 📂 Deserialization LoadTerrainFromFile public static bool LoadTerrainFromFile(string filePath, Entity terrainEntity, EntityManager entityManager, CustomDeserializerCallback customDeserializer) Loads terrain data from a file and applies it to the target terrain entity. 🔓 Deserialization Methods Deserialize(Stream stream, ...) Deserialize(BinaryReader reader, ...) ReadVersion1(BinaryReader reader, ...) Reads and applies the terrain settings. Matches type hashes to existing component types. Deserializes data into existing component objects using: ReadSurfaceData ReadCellItemsData ReadCellEntitiesData ReadTerrainByteAreas 🧩 Supported Layers The following managed components are supported out of the box: Component Type Write Method Read Method HexSurfaceLayer WriteSurfaceData ReadSurfaceData CellItemsLayer WriteCellItemsData ReadCellItemsData CellEntitiesLayer WriteCellEntitiesData ReadCellEntitiesData HexByteAreasLayer WriteTerrainByteAreas ReadTerrainByteAreas 🧪 Custom Serialization CustomSerializerCallback public delegate bool CustomSerializerCallback(BinaryWriter writer, object componentObject); Called during write if the user wants to handle custom logic. CustomDeserializerCallback public delegate bool CustomDeserializerCallback(BinaryReader reader, Type componentType, HexTerrainSettings terrainSettings); Called during read if the user wants to deserialize custom logic. 📘 Usage Example HexTerrainSerializer.SaveTerrainToFile("Assets/terrain.bin", terrainEntity, entityManager, MyCustomSerialize); HexTerrainSerializer.LoadTerrainFromFile("Assets/terrain.bin", terrainEntity, entityManager, MyCustomDeserialize); 🧱 Binary Format Summary Terrain format version (int) HexTerrainSettings struct (int2, floats, enums) Component Type Hash (ulong) Native list data (length + binary contents) ✅ Best Practices Always complete all jobs (CompleteAllJobs) before saving to ensure consistency. Keep serialization layer-specific logic in their respective data layers. Use the custom serializer to support user-defined or experimental components.

terrain-surface-rendering.html.title: 📦 Surface Rendering | Hex Terrains Framework
terrain-surface-rendering.html.summary: 📦 Surface Rendering The Hex Terrains Framework supports performant rendering of surface layers (like ground or water) using ECS-compatible systems and highly optimized chunk-based rendering workflows. This section explains how rendering works, what components are involved, and how meshes are dynamically generated and drawn for visible terrain chunks. 🔁 Rendering Workflow Overview Surface rendering is split into three main phases: Create Render Data The CreateSurfaceRenderDataSystem is responsible for creating a HexSurfaceRenderLayer instance tied to a specific HexSurfaceLayer. This object holds all the render-related data structures including chunk meshes, mesh sources, and render configuration. Calculate Mesh Sources (Verts, UV, tris, etc.) The CalcGroundMeshSourcesSystem system calculates mesh data for visible chunks to be later copied into the chunk meshes (regular Unity Mesh). Generate Mesh Data The CalcSurfaceMeshesSystem converts the intermediate MeshSource data (generated earlier by other systems like CalcGroundMeshSourcesSystem) into actual Unity Mesh objects per chunk. Only dirty or changed chunks are reprocessed. Render Meshes The RenderHexSurfaceSystem uses Unity’s Graphics.DrawMesh to efficiently render only the visible chunks for the current camera using instancing and render config materials. 🏗 CreateSurfaceRenderLayerSystem public class CreateSurfaceRenderLayerSystem<TRequest, TSurfaceLayer, TRenderData, TRenderConfig> : SystemBase Purpose: Initializes the render data structure when a TRequest component is present on a terrain entity. Output: Attaches a TRenderData component with: Render settings from the request. Render config asset. Camera reference for rendering. Example Output: Adds HexGroundRenderLayer or HexWaterRenderLayer. 🧩 Render data includes: ChunkMeshSources (procedural mesh definitions) ChunkMeshes (final Mesh instances) RenderConfig (materials and shadow settings) 【Source: CreateSurfaceRenderLayerSystem.cs】 🧬 CalcSurfaceMeshesSystem public class CalcSurfaceMeshesSystem<TSurfaceData, TRenderData> : SystemBase Purpose: Builds Unity Mesh objects from procedural MeshSource data for each chunk. Key Features: Skips work if nothing is dirty. Processes only marked dirty chunks via GeneratedMeshIndexes. Fills meshes using MeshSource.FillMesh() and stores them in the render layer. Optimization: Once processed, dirty flags are reset to avoid redundant work. 🛠 Example: meshSources[chunkIndex].FillMesh(chunkMesh); 【Source: CalcSurfaceMeshesSystem.cs】 🖼 RenderHexSurfaceSystem public class RenderHexSurfaceSystem<TSurfaceData, TRenderData> : SystemBase Purpose: Draws all visible chunk meshes using Graphics.DrawMesh. Features: Uses ChunkVisibility to skip non-visible chunks. Supports view mode switching via HexTerrainViewMode. Can draw multi-material meshes using submesh indices. 🔍 Pseudocode: foreach (chunkIndex in visibleChunks) if (chunk is visible) DrawMesh(chunkMeshes[chunkIndex], transform, material) Supports: Shadows (IsCastShadows, IsReceiveShadows) and instanced draw calls. 【Source: RenderHexSurfaceSystem.cs】 🧾 Supporting Components Component / System Purpose HexSurfaceRenderLayer Holds all mesh/render data for surface MeshSource Procedural mesh buffer (verts, tris, uvs) ChunksGridData.ChunkVisibility Visibility status and transform for each chunk HexTerrainViewMode View mode index for rendering config HexSurfaceRenderConfig Materials, shadow settings, etc. ✅ Summary The surface rendering pipeline in Hex Terrains Framework is designed for maximum performance and visual clarity, dynamically processing and rendering only the chunks that are visible. The system is highly modular, allowing surfaces like ground and water to be rendered using shared logic, with configuration driven by ECS components and per-layer settings.

terrain-surfaces.html.title: 🌍 Terrain Surfaces | Hex Terrains Framework
terrain-surfaces.html.summary: 🌍 Terrain Surfaces Hex Terrains Framework supports multiple surface types (like ground or water), each implemented as a HexSurfaceLayer. These surfaces are responsible for storing key data such as height, biomes, and render information. Surfaces are extensible, fully ECS-compatible, and processed with DOTS for maximum performance. Surface Types Each surface type is implemented as a class that inherits from HexSurfaceLayer. The primary concrete implementations include: HexGroundLayer – for terrain ground surface (elevation, terrain biomes). WaterSurfaceLayer (not shown here, but supported similarly). Each surface has associated systems to handle metric calculation and rendering-related preprocessing. 🧱 Structure of a Surface Layer Each HexSurfaceLayer holds multiple data layers, such as: Data Layer Purpose HeightMap Stores per-cell elevation BiomesMap Stores biome index per cell CellColorMap Stores visualized colors for each cell CellMetrics Stores combined metrics derived from height + biome BiomeColors A palette for converting biome index to color All of these layers are implemented as DataLayer or ChunkedDataLayer objects and benefit from read/write dependency tracking and chunk-level dirty maps for efficient job scheduling. 🧪 Data Generation and Setup Surfaces can be initialized via authoring components in the Unity Editor. For example: Example: HexGroundLayerAuthoring public class HexGroundLayerAuthoring : HexSurfaceLayerAuthoring {} When baked by HexGroundDataBaker, this authoring component: Sets up height, biomes, and color palette. Adds the HexGroundColorPalette buffer to the terrain entity. Schedules a CreateHexGroundLayerRequest. public struct CreateHexGroundLayerRequest : ICreateHexSurfaceRequest, IComponentData This request is then picked up by systems to construct the ECS-side surface representation. ⚙️ Simulation and Updates Color Map Generation: CalcCellBiomeColorsSystem<T> This system: Compares dirty flags between biomes and color maps. Combines chunk-level dirty grids. Schedules a CalculateBiomesColorMapJob or CalculateWaterColorMapJob. Writes biome color to CellColorMap using the defined palette. The system ensures color maps update only when needed, and processes data in jobs chunk-by-chunk. Metrics Calculation: CalcCellMetricsSystem<T> Surface metrics such as slope, average height, or relative biome data are calculated here. Depends on HeightMap and BiomesMap. Uses ChunkDirtyGrid to identify regions needing recalculation. Populates CellMetrics (metrics and cell position data). Specialized implementation: public partial class CalcGroundCellMetricsSystem : CalcCellMetricsSystem<HexGroundLayer> 🔄 Runtime Behavior Systems are designed to work independently per terrain, which allows multi-terrain setups. Surfaces automatically react to changes in their layers (e.g., biome or heightmap changes) via their dirty flags and dependency tracking. 🌈 Color Palette System For visual feedback (e.g., biomes displayed in the minimap or by coloring cells on terrain): Each surface has a color palette (e.g., HexGroundColorPalette). The palette is used during biome color map job execution. Supports easy customization and visualization without needing shader-side logic. 🧩 Custom Surfaces To create a custom surface: Derive from HexSurfaceLayer. Create an authoring component and baker. Implement a data creation request (ICreateHexSurfaceRequest). Add custom systems for metric or render preparation as needed. Here's a structured documentation section for the Terrain Surfaces system in your Hex Terrains Framework: Terrain Surfaces Hex Terrains Framework supports multiple surface types (e.g., ground, water) using a flexible and extensible layer system. Each surface is implemented as a specialized HexSurfaceLayer and may store height data, biome information, color maps, and associated rendering data. This section details how terrain surfaces are constructed, managed, raycasted, and updated. Overview A HexSurface is a conceptual layer of the terrain, such as the ground or water. Each one is implemented via: A derived class from HexSurfaceLayer A HeightMapDataLayer for cell heights (as byte, scaled to world meters) A CellBiomesDataLayer for storing biome types per cell A CellColorsDataLayer for coloring the surface, updated based on biomes or other logic A HexTerrainRenderData layer to render the surface mesh Example surface layers: HexGroundLayer (ground surface) HexWaterLayer (custom surface type, if added) Each implements ICreateHexSurfaceDataRequest or uses associated request structs for instantiation Layer Creation Surfaces are initialized by systems such as CreateHexGroundLayerRequest and CreateHexSurfaceRequestArgs, usually via authoring components like HexGroundLayerAuthoring or HexSurfaceLayerAuthoring. These components describe what kind of surface to create and associate them with a terrain entity. Example Setup Flow HexGroundLayerAuthoring -> CreateHexGroundLayerRequest → System receives request → Creates HexGroundLayer → Initializes DataLayers (HeightMap, Biomes, Colors) Cleanup Each surface is cleaned every frame (if visible) to clear dirty flags or release temporary resources. Base class: CleanupHexSurfaceLayerSystem<TSurface> Example implementation: CleanupHexGroundLayerSystem public class CleanupHexGroundLayerSystem : CleanupHexSurfaceLayerSystem<HexGroundLayer> { protected override void OnUpdate() { ... } } The system checks HexTerrainVisibility.Value before calling surface.CleanupAsync(). Surface Color Map Calculation The biomes map drives the visual appearance of terrain via CalculateBiomesColorMapJob. This job: Iterates over each cell in parallel Skips clean (non-dirty) chunks Maps the biome index (byte) to a Color32 using a palette Writes results into CellColorsDataLayer if (cellValue < Colors.Length) CellColorMap[index] = Colors[cellValue]; else CellColorMap[index] = DefaultColor; This allows efficient color map recalculation per chunk. Raycasting Two raycasting jobs exist for interaction and tooling: RaycastHexTerrainJob Raycasts against a single surface's heightmap. It: Iterates along the ray by steps Converts world coordinates to hex cell index Checks if the point is under the surface's height If so, it writes a HexTerrainRaycastData containing: IsHit HitPosition CellCoord, CellIndex, ChunkIndex, ChunkCoord RaycastHexTerrain2Job Works similarly, but checks two surfaces simultaneously (e.g., ground and water) and picks the one with higher height at each cell. var rawHeight = max(Heightmap1[cellIndex], Heightmap2[cellIndex]); This enables correct behavior for raycasts involving layered terrain. Terrain Metrics The CalcHexCellMetricsJob and CalcCellMetricsSystem compute per-cell properties like slope, height, and elevation, used for physics, rendering, or gameplay logic. These systems run after terrain data changes and update internal terrain state accordingly. Summary Hex Terrain Surfaces provide an efficient and extensible way to represent elevation, biomes, and visual data. Each surface is ECS-native and fully integrated into the simulation loop, using chunked data layers, dirty tracking, and job scheduling for high performance. Whether you're rendering a mountain range or simulating ocean waves, HexSurfaceLayer is the foundation that supports terrain realism in the framework.

user-interface.html.title: User Interface concepts | Hex Terrains Framework
user-interface.html.summary: User Interface concepts 🧩 UI Binding System in Hex Terrains Framework The UI in Hex Terrains Framework is built on Unity UI Toolkit and uses a data-driven binding system that seamlessly synchronizes UI screens with underlying runtime data. This system ensures UI elements always reflect the current application state, and allows runtime tools (like terrain brushes, minimaps, and tool selectors) to respond to user input with minimal boilerplate. 🧱 Core Concepts Component Role UIDataSource Base class for all bindable data. Tracks changes using a Version. IViewDataReceiver<T> Interface for screens to receive and apply data sources. UIScreen<T> Base class for all UI screens, supports binding and updating. ToolSettingsScreen<T> Generic base for tool-specific UI panels. MinimapScreenBase Base for minimap UI, receives view data updates from systems. 📊 Data Binding with UIDataSource All data exposed to UI inherits from UIDataSource. This abstract class handles: Change detection via a Version counter Dirty tracking using MarkDirty() UI invalidation with CommitChanges() public abstract class UIDataSource : ICommitChanges { public long Version; public virtual void MarkDirty() => Version++; public virtual void CommitChanges() => MarkDirty(); } When a value changes, CommitChanges() increments the Version, signaling UI Toolkit to rebind affected elements. 🔁 View Data Lifecycle A screen receives a data object via SetViewData(T viewData) The screen assigns the data to its root visual element's .dataSource UI Toolkit auto-binds fields based on [CreateProperty] attributes public virtual void SetViewData(TSettings viewData) { _viewData = viewData; if (TryGetRootElement(out var rootElement)) { rootElement.dataSource = viewData; } } This flow is defined in ToolSettingsScreen<T> and reused across all UI panels. 🧰 Example: Tool Settings Panel public class UniversalToolSettingsScreen : ToolSettingsScreen<UserToolSettingsDataSource> { } Binds to UserToolSettingsDataSource, which is a UIDataSource Automatically reflects settings like brush size, tool parameters, and visibility Changes to settings (e.g., via sliders or dropdowns) update the bound data and propagate to the active user tool 🗺️ Example: Minimap UI The minimap UI is backed by MinimapScreenDataSource, a subclass of UIDataSource. Key properties: [CreateProperty] public List<Texture2D> ColorMapTextures; [CreateProperty] public List<DisplayStyle> ColorMapTextureVisibilities; [CreateProperty] public Vector2 CameraNormalizedPosition; When SetColorTextures(...) or SetViewMode(...) is called in MinimapScreenBase, it updates the data source and commits changes: ViewData.SetVisibleTextureIndexes(visibleIndexes); ViewData.CommitChanges(); This triggers an immediate UI refresh showing the correct textures and view modes. 🧪 UI Message Routing (Optional) The IViewDataReceiver<T> and base IViewDataReceiver interfaces support message routing and generalized UI communication. ✅ Benefits Declarative, low-code UI architecture Automatic UI refresh on data changes Clean separation between logic and presentation Highly extensible and testable 🧱 UI Toolkit Custom Controls and Data Templates In addition to core screen and data binding infrastructure, the Hex Terrains Framework includes a powerful set of custom UI Toolkit components to streamline data-driven UI development. These components support dynamic layout, list rendering, event handling, and runtime template selection. 🔘 UIButton: Unified Button Binding The UIButton component enhances Unity's standard Button by supporting multiple binding strategies for click handling: [CreateProperty] public object OnClick { get; set; } [CreateProperty] public string OnClickPath { get; set; } Supported click targets include: Action UnityEvent UIButtonDataSource (with an OnClick action) Property path bindings (using OnClickPath) This flexibility allows UI to invoke methods on view models or data sources declaratively. 📃 SimpleListView: Static Template Lists The SimpleListView displays a list of items using a single VisualTreeAsset template: [CreateProperty] public VisualTreeAsset ItemTemplate { get; set; } [CreateProperty] public IList itemsSource { get; set; } For each item in itemsSource: A view is instantiated using ItemTemplate Its .dataSource is assigned If the view implements ICommitChanges, it is refreshed automatically This is ideal for simple collections with consistent UI layout. 🧩 UIListView: Event-Driven Selection UIListView extends Unity’s native ListView with enhanced selection binding. You can assign: UnityEvent<IEnumerable<object>> UnityEvent<int> Action<int> or Action<IEnumerable<object>> All are invoked automatically when the user changes selection. public object OnSelectionChange { get; set; } 🎭 Template Selection System The framework supports data-driven UI templates using: TemplateSelectorConfig: Base for defining default templates TemplateSelectorConfigByType: Maps C# types to specific templates DataTemplateConfig: Stores the mapping between type and VisualTreeAsset This system allows runtime UI to render heterogeneous data models with distinct views based on data type. public override VisualTreeAsset GetTemplateForData<TData>(TData data) { return GetTemplateForType(typeof(TData)); } 🧱 TemplateSelectorElement: Dynamic UI Rendering TemplateSelectorElement dynamically selects and instantiates a view template at runtime based on the data it is bound to. How it works: Retrieves a data object from the UI hierarchy using GetHierarchicalDataSourceContext Selects a template via a TemplateSelectorConfig Creates and binds a view using the selected template Automatically updates when data changes or when reattached to panel This mechanism is ideal for modular and polymorphic UIs such as: Properties panels for different object types Inspector-style interfaces Minimap overlays with customizable visuals 💡 Summary Component Purpose UIButton Data-bound click handling with path and object support SimpleListView Fast list rendering using one template UIListView Flexible list view with event-driven selection TemplateSelectorConfig Maps data types to UI templates TemplateSelectorElement Renders data using a selected template at runtime

user-tools.html.title: 🖌️ In-Game Terrain Editor | Hex Terrains Framework
user-tools.html.summary: 🖌️ In-Game Terrain Editor Overview The Hex Terrains Framework features a powerful in-game terrain editor designed with a Photoshop-like workflow in mind. It supports: Brush-based editing with size, opacity, and color control Modular tools for deforming terrain, painting areas, placing objects, and more A runtime state machine to manage tools Full UI Toolkit integration via a shared UI system Clean separation between UI code and ECS-based terrain data 🎛️ User Tool System Architecture Each editor tool is a state within a UserToolStateMachine, allowing seamless switching between editing modes. Key Components Component Description UserToolStateMachine Runtime state machine managing tool transitions UserToolStateBase Base class for all tool states; handles activation, brush setup, view mode IHexTerrainAPI Interface injected into tools to access terrain editing APIs UserToolSettings Data-driven brush/tool parameters IUISystemAPI UI integration layer for editor panels and toolbars 🔁 Tool Lifecycle Each tool derives from UserToolStateBase and can optionally: Initialize a UI panel (ShowSettingsScreen) Activate a custom brush with settings Switch terrain view modes Apply edits using ApplyBrush(...) Example Lifecycle Flow [Tool Selected] ↓ PrepareToRun() ↓ Set View Mode / Show Brush ↓ Tick() – per-frame updates ↓ ApplyBrush(...) – on user input ↓ PrepareToStop() – restore view mode, hide UI 🖼️ Tool Example: Deform Ground Class: DeformGroundUserToolState This tool deforms terrain height based on mouse input, key modifiers, and brush size. public class DeformGroundUserToolState : DeformHeightUserToolState<HexGroundLayer> { public override int UserToolType => (int)UserToolTypes.GroundDeformation; } Modifier Keys Key Effect LeftAlt Inverts height delta LeftShift Applies turbo strength 🗺️ Tool Example: Paint Countries Class: PaintCountriesUserToolState This tool paints area indices (such as countries) onto cells, optionally constrained by elevation. public class PaintCountriesUserToolState : PaintAreasUserToolState<HexCountriesLayer, HexGroundLayer> { public override int UserToolType => (int)UserToolTypes.CountriesPainting; } Settings Index – area index (byte 0–255) Min Cell Height – skip cells below this elevation Max Cell Height – skip cells above this elevation 🧠 IHexTerrainAPI – Bridging Tools and Terrain The IHexTerrainAPI allows tools to interact with terrain layers outside ECS systems: public interface IHexTerrainAPI { void SetIsVisibleBrush(bool isVisible); void SetBrushSize(int size); void SetBrushColor(Color32 color); void SetIsResizableBrush(bool isResizable); int GetViewMode(); void SetViewMode(byte mode); byte GetCellHeight<TSurfaceLayer>(int cellIndex) where TSurfaceLayer : HexSurfaceLayer; // ... other helper methods } This ensures tools are lightweight, testable, and do not manipulate ECS state directly. 🧩 Creating a New Tool To implement a new terrain editing tool: Inherit from UserToolStateBase or a derived class like BrushUserToolState Implement ApplyBrush(...) with your editing logic Set a unique UserToolType ID Register the tool in your state machine (Optional) Provide a UI panel by calling ShowSettingsScreen Template public class MyCustomToolState : BrushUserToolState<SomeLayer> { public override int UserToolType => (int)UserToolTypes.MyTool; public MyCustomToolState(IHexTerrainAPI hexTerrainAPI) : base(hexTerrainAPI) { } public override bool ApplyBrush(...) { // Custom logic here } } 📐 Brushes & Cursors Brush visuals and interaction are controlled via IHexTerrainAPI: Size Color Opacity Visibility Resizability All brush properties are dynamically adjusted based on tool and user input. 🧠 Tool Settings UI Tools can define custom settings through data-driven UserToolSettingsDataSource: DataSource.AddValue(new UserToolParameterDataSource<int> { Name = "Min Cell Height", MinValue = 0, MaxValue = 255, Value = 3, IsClampValue = true, IsVisible = true }); The UI system automatically binds these parameters to in-game panels using a common UIScreen and IViewDataReceiver. 🧼 Cleanup and Memory Safety All tools implement: Dispose() for cleanup PrepareToStart() to prepare tool for work and show UI Tick() to apply per-frame logic PrepareToStop() to revert view modes and hide UI and more (see UserToolStateBase) 🖌 Brush-Based Terrain Editing The BrushUserTool system powers the in-game Photoshop-like editing experience within the Hex Terrains Framework. It allows real-time, cell-level modifications of terrain layers using a dynamic, customizable brush. Each tool is implemented as a state in a user tool state machine and inherits from a shared foundation: BrushUserToolState. Key Features Adjustable brush size and opacity Unified API for diverse operations (e.g., painting countries, applying heightmaps, stamping objects) Tool-specific logic via overrideable brush application methods Data-driven settings exposed via UI Supports undo/redo, smooth user interactions, and multi-step operations 🔧 Base Class: BrushUserToolState The core abstract base class: BrushUserToolState<TBrushTarget, TDataSource, TUIScreen> TBrushTarget: The layer type affected (e.g., HexSurfaceLayer, CellEntitiesLayer) TDataSource: A class describing editable settings (usually UserToolSettingsDataSource) TUIScreen: The settings panel (usually UniversalToolSettingsScreen) Example Implementations Tool Inherits From Purpose ApplyHeightmapUserToolState BrushUserToolState<HexSurfaceLayer, ...> Paints heightmap values onto terrain cells AutoPaintUserToolState BrushUserToolState<HexSurfaceLayer, ...> Auto-assigns biomes based on elevation PaintCountriesUserToolState PaintAreasUserToolState<HexCountriesLayer, ...> Assigns country indices per cell LevelTerrainUserToolState BrushUserToolState<HexSurfaceLayer, ...> Sets cells to a specific elevation StampUserToolStateBase BrushUserToolState<...> Copies cell data from one area to another 🔁 Brush Lifecycle Each frame while a brush is active: Cursor location is evaluated (HexTerrainAPI.GetCellCoordUnderCursor()). Affected cells within brush radius are gathered. ApplyBrush(...) is invoked for each cell. Layer-specific logic (e.g., biome assignment, height change, object stamping) is applied. UI settings are updated if necessary (e.g., when reading a value). 🧠 User-Defined Parameters Each brush tool can expose user-facing parameters: DataSource.AddValue(new UserToolParameterDataSource<int> { Name = "Elevation", Value = 0, MinValue = 0, MaxValue = 255, IsVisible = true, }); These parameters are shown in the editor UI and persisted during the session. ✍️ Overriding ApplyBrush Every brush tool must override ApplyBrush: public override bool ApplyBrush(int brushMode, int2 cellCoord, int cellIndex, TBrushTarget target, int mouseButton) For example, in ApplyHeightmapUserToolState, the method reads a value from a texture and updates the terrain height: var pixel = Heightmap.GetPixelBilinear(progress.x, progress.y); var height = (byte)math.clamp(pixel.r * scale * 255 + offset, 0, 255); brushTarget.SetCellHeight(cellIndex, height); 🧬 Extending BrushUserTool To create a custom brush tool: Inherit from BrushUserToolState<TBrushTarget, TDataSource, TUIScreen> Override InitDefaultSettings() to register UI parameters. Override ApplyBrush(...) with logic for applying edits. Register your tool in the state machine (UserToolStateMachine.SwitchStateByUserToolType(...)). 🛠️ HexTerrainAPI: Default Implementation of IHexTerrainAPI The HexTerrainAPI class is the default implementation of the IHexTerrainAPI interface, designed to bridge runtime user tools (e.g., brush operations) with ECS-based HexTerrain data structures. It provides a standardized way for tool states to interact with terrain data, access brush settings, UI screens, and read/write values from data layers such as heightmaps, biomes, cell entities, and areas — all without requiring direct access to the EntityManager. 🔑 Purpose Acts as a facade over the EntityManager, abstracting terrain access logic. Enables tools (like BrushUserToolState) to: Modify terrain data (e.g., deform terrain, paint biomes). Read/write brush settings (size, opacity, visibility). Manage terrain lifecycle (create, destroy, resize, save/load). Interact with UI (via injected IUISystemAPI). Is injectable into tool states as IHexTerrainAPI. 🔧 Core Components Property Description EntityManager ECS context for terrain access. TerrainEntity Current active terrain entity. UserToolEntity Tool controller entity (provides prefab configs, settings). UISystemAPI Interface to manage UI screens (create, destroy, retrieve). 🧱 Terrain Access & Manipulation You can access and modify ECS terrain data safely through these functions: Generic Data Layer Access TDataLayer GetDataLayer<TDataLayer>() where TDataLayer : class; bool IsLayerSupported<TDataLayer>() where TDataLayer : class; Heightmap / Biome Access byte? GetCellHeight<TSurface>() / SetCellHeight<TSurface>() byte? GetCellBiome<TSurface>() / SetCellBiome<TSurface>() Cell Items / Entities CellItem? GetCellItem<T>() / bool SetCellItem<T>() CellEntity? GetCellEntity<T>() / bool SetCellEntity<T>() Areas byte? GetCellArea<T>() / bool SetCellArea<T>() Raycasting HexTerrainRaycastData? GetRaycastData() int? GetCellIndexUnderCursor() int2? GetCellCoordUnderCursor() 🎨 Brush Manipulation HexTerrainAPI provides full access to brush properties: Property Methods Size GetBrushSize(), SetBrushSize(int) Opacity GetBrushOpacity(), SetBrushOpacity(float) Visibility GetIsVisibleBrush(), SetIsVisibleBrush(bool) Resizability GetIsResizableBrush(), SetIsResizableBrush(bool) Color GetBrushColor(), SetBrushColor(Color32) View Mode GetViewMode(), SetViewMode(byte) View GetBrushView() 🗺️ Terrain Lifecycle Management Operation Method Save / Load SaveTerrain(path), LoadTerrain(path) Resize ResizeTerrain(int2) Destroy DestroyTerrain(entity) Create CreateNewTerrainEntity(prefab) CreateNewTerrain(config, settings) 🖼️ UI Integration Operation Method Create screen CreateUIScreen<T>() Get screen GetUIScreen<T>() Get or create GetOrCreateUIScreen<T>() Destroy screen DestroyUIScreen<T>() / DestroyUIScreen(UIScreen) 🧩 Extensibility Developers can: Use this class as-is. Subclass it to extend behavior. Implement IHexTerrainAPI from scratch for alternative logic. This makes HexTerrainAPI both powerful and flexible, fitting a wide range of in-game editor use cases.
